Title: Health & Wellness: A Different Way to Approach Your Wedding-Day Goals
Author: Carrie Denny Whitcraft
Summary: This wedding‑focused article borrows the design‑thinking approach to goal setting. It urges readers to identify the deeper reasons behind their wedding‑day goals. Dani Singer, CEO of Fit2Go, explains that thinking beyond surface‑level metrics (like pounds lost or body‑fat percentage) helps people find what really matters. He says that when clients imagine how reaching a fitness goal will affect other areas of life (confidence, energy, well‑being), they’re more likely to succeed(https://www.phillymag.com/philadelphia-wedding/2017/03/08/health-wellness-a-different-way-to-approach-your-wedding-day-goals/#:~:text=,to%20the%20Personal%20Trainer%20Development).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘Think into the future—six months or a year from now … maybe you lost 10 pounds or lowered your body‑fat percentage. Bigger than those facts themselves, try to get yourself into that mindset of how that will affect other areas of your life’(https://www.phillymag.com/philadelphia-wedding/2017/03/08/health-wellness-a-different-way-to-approach-your-wedding-day-goals/#:~:text=,to%20the%20Personal%20Trainer%20Development).

Title: This Instagram Star Says She Actually Doesn't Do Cardio
Author: Korin Miller
Summary: SELF asked fitness experts whether skipping cardio is a good idea. Dani Singer explained that high‑intensity interval training (HIIT) mixes anaerobic strength work with aerobic cardio. Because HIIT cycles include rest periods, many people don’t count it as ‘cardio,’ yet it still burns fat efficiently. Singer also warned that completely eliminating steady‑state cardio isn’t wise — traditional cardio offers heart‑health benefits and should be included at least once a week(https://www.self.com/story/sophie-guidolin-cardio#:~:text=High,state%2C%20relentless%20activity%2C%20he%20says)(https://www.self.com/story/sophie-guidolin-cardio#:~:text=your%20overall%20cardiovascular%20health,he%20says).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer said HIIT ‘will help burn fat and save time, but it doesn’t necessarily fall under the category of “cardio” since it’s not steady‑state, relentless activity’(https://www.self.com/story/sophie-guidolin-cardio#:~:text=High,state%2C%20relentless%20activity%2C%20he%20says). He added that traditional cardio provides heart benefits you won’t get from strength training alone, so it’s worth including it in the mix(https://www.self.com/story/sophie-guidolin-cardio#:~:text=your%20overall%20cardiovascular%20health,he%20says).

Title: 4 Differences in How Cardio and Strength Affect Your Health
Author: Ruben Castaneda & K. Aleisha Fetters
Site: U.S. News & World Report (republished by Yahoo)
Summary: This article compares cardiovascular exercise with strength training. Dani Singer notes that intensity matters more than the exercise modality and argues that weight training is the most effective way to reduce body‑fat percentage. He clarifies that weight loss and fat loss are different: being in a calorie deficit will burn fat and muscle unless you send your body the message that it needs muscle via strength training(https://www.yahoo.com/news/4-differences-cardio-strength-affect-health-200038971.html#:~:text=Below%2C%20experts%20share%20the%20unique,the%20best%20of%20both%20workouts).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says intensity is key and that ‘strength training is the most effective type of exercise to reduce body fat percentage’(https://www.yahoo.com/news/4-differences-cardio-strength-affect-health-200038971.html#:~:text=Below%2C%20experts%20share%20the%20unique,the%20best%20of%20both%20workouts). He explains that people care more about being lean than about the number on the scale and that strength training tells the body to maintain muscle while burning fat(https://www.yahoo.com/news/4-differences-cardio-strength-affect-health-200038971.html#:~:text=It%27s%20important%20to%20distinguish%20the,will%20also%20burn%20muscle%20tissue).

Title: Short on Time? Try a HIIT Workout
Author: Erica Patino
Summary: A guide to high‑intensity interval training (HIIT) for people over 40. Dani Singer explains that HIIT alternates anaerobic strength work with aerobic cardio. These cycles allow you to hit 80–90 % of your maximum heart rate during work periods and recover at lower intensity. Singer says HIIT originally gained popularity because it burns more calories for weight loss, but research now shows that it also improves mobility and body composition(https://darioconnect.com/feed/articles/how-women-over-40-can-start-high-intensity-interval-training/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CWhen%20people%20say%20%E2%80%98high,%E2%80%9D).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer describes HIIT as ‘a mix of anaerobic and aerobic work’ and notes that it became popular because it burns more calories but now we know it improves mobility too(https://darioconnect.com/feed/articles/how-women-over-40-can-start-high-intensity-interval-training/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CWhen%20people%20say%20%E2%80%98high,%E2%80%9D).

Title: 14 Things that Happen When You Start a Beginner Weight‑Lifting Workout
Author: Marissa Laliberte
Summary: This list article describes benefits of starting a weight‑lifting routine. Dani Singer tells readers that lifting weights improves energy efficiency so everyday tasks (walking stairs, cooking) become easier(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=You%E2%80%99ll%20have%20more%20energy). He notes that improved posture is a ‘side benefit’ of strength training because contracting muscles makes people stand taller and can relieve joint or spinal pain(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=Confidence%20isn%E2%80%99t%20the%20only%20reason,other%20ways%20to%20improve%20posture). Singer also says weight lifting feels more engaging than cardio and empowers people because circuits and fun exercises make it less of a chore(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=People%20are%20often%20surprised%20by,the%20importance%20of%20strength%20training).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says strength training ‘improves your body’s efficiency—everything else becomes easier’(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=You%E2%80%99ll%20have%20more%20energy). He adds that proper weight lifting makes people stand straighter and relieves pain by balancing de‑conditioned muscles(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=Confidence%20isn%E2%80%99t%20the%20only%20reason,other%20ways%20to%20improve%20posture), and he points out that people often prefer weight circuits because they’re more fun and empowering than cardio(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/strength-training/beginner-strength-training/#:~:text=People%20are%20often%20surprised%20by,the%20importance%20of%20strength%20training).

Title: 9 Reasons You’re Not Getting Results from Strength Training
Author: Melissa Rudy
Summary: This piece lists mistakes that sabotage strength‑training progress. Dani Singer warns that performing the same routine repeatedly causes the body to adapt and plateau. He believes in ‘muscle confusion’—changing exercises or variables to keep muscles guessing(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/All/9%20Reasons%20Youre%20Not%20Getting%20Results%20from%20Strength%20Training#:~:text=Singer%20www,getting%20stronger). However, he cautions against changing workouts too frequently; instead, he recommends modifying routines only after you’ve mastered them or when progress stalls(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/All/9%20Reasons%20Youre%20Not%20Getting%20Results%20from%20Strength%20Training#:~:text=,stops%20producing%20the%20desired%20results).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says that if you’ve stopped making progress because you’ve been following the exact same routine for years, ‘maybe it’s time to learn a new exercise’(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/All/9%20Reasons%20Youre%20Not%20Getting%20Results%20from%20Strength%20Training#:~:text=Singer%20www,getting%20stronger). He cautions that varying workouts too often can backfire and advises changing routines only when you’ve mastered them or they stop producing results(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/All/9%20Reasons%20Youre%20Not%20Getting%20Results%20from%20Strength%20Training#:~:text=,stops%20producing%20the%20desired%20results).

Title: 5 Tips for Learning a New Exercise
Author: Ruben Castaneda
Summary: U.S. News asked experts how to master unfamiliar exercises. Dani Singer tells readers that learning a new movement is about technique; the more you learn, the more you realize you don’t know(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=exercise%20%2C%20like%20Carruth%20did,less%20wasted%20energy%2C%20he%20says). He advises people to view exercise as a journey and cautions that expecting to be great immediately will lead to failure(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=a%20new%20exercise%2C%20Singer%20says,view%20it%20as%20a%20journey). Singer recommends working with a certified personal trainer—many clients need help with form or motivation—and stresses that proper technique prevents wasted energy and injury(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=Consider%20hiring%20a%20personal%20trainer,to%20get%20started%20on%20a)(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=Be%20sure%20you%20have%20a,performed%20walk%20you%20through%20it).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘If you expect to be great right away, for sure you’ll fail,’ Singer says, urging people to see exercise as a journey(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=a%20new%20exercise%2C%20Singer%20says,view%20it%20as%20a%20journey). He notes that mastering technique makes movement more efficient and that everyone can benefit from at least a month with a qualified trainer to learn proper form(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=Consider%20hiring%20a%20personal%20trainer,to%20get%20started%20on%20a)(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-09-10/5-tips-for-learning-a-new-exercise#:~:text=Be%20sure%20you%20have%20a,performed%20walk%20you%20through%20it).

Title: How to Eat (and Exercise) to Get Six‑Pack Abs
Author: Ruben Castaneda
Summary: This article explains that achieving visible abdominal muscles requires both diet and training. Dani Singer says a calorie deficit, adequate protein and strength training are the key factors that affect body composition—not the specific foods eaten(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=Job%20one%20when%20trying%20to,determine%20how%20your%20body%20looks). He stresses prioritizing protein to maintain muscle mass while losing fat(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=sugar%2C%20be%20sure%20to%20consume,Lean%20meats%2C%20skinless) and recommends weighted crunches and sit‑ups to strengthen the rectus abdominis; everyone technically has a ‘six‑pack,’ but fat loss and training make it visible(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=5). Singer also urges readers to seek guidance from qualified professionals to avoid pseudoscience(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=A%20great%20fitness%20professional%20will,he%20says).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer notes that the sources of your food don’t affect body composition as much as total calories and macronutrients(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=Job%20one%20when%20trying%20to,determine%20how%20your%20body%20looks). He emphasizes that consuming enough protein helps maintain muscle while encouraging the body to burn fat(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=sugar%2C%20be%20sure%20to%20consume,Lean%20meats%2C%20skinless)(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=If%20you%27re%20in%20a%20caloric,Singer%20says) and points out that everyone has a six‑pack—the goal is to build and reveal it through strength training and fat loss(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=5). He cautions readers to consult experts to avoid fitness pseudoscience(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-08-30/how-to-eat-and-exercise-to-get-six-pack-abs#:~:text=A%20great%20fitness%20professional%20will,he%20says).

Title: 5 Workout Strategies for Trans Women
Author: Ruben Castaneda
Summary: U.S. News explores fitness considerations for trans women. Dani Singer agrees that glute bridges help build glute muscle mass and stresses that specificity matters—the more precise your goal (marathon vs. bodybuilding), the better your program(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=Whatever%20type%20of%20changes%20they,in%20your%20glutes%2C%20Singer%20says)(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=specific%20the%20goal%2C%20the%20better%2C,Singer%20says). He notes that many trainers offer in‑home or online sessions and says he frequently travels to clients’ homes(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=training%20online%3B%20Flizanes%20works%20with,the%20homes%20of%20many%20clients). Singer advises adjusting workouts when you hit a plateau and emphasizes perfecting form; if you can’t perform an exercise with good form, decrease the reps and focus on technique(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=you%27ll%20reach%20a%20fitness%20plateau,do%20it%20with%20good%20form).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says the more specific your fitness goal, the better, because different goals require different programs(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=specific%20the%20goal%2C%20the%20better%2C,Singer%20says). He notes that he often trains clients at home and that virtual options exist(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=training%20online%3B%20Flizanes%20works%20with,the%20homes%20of%20many%20clients). When clients hit a plateau, he suggests adjusting the workout and prioritizing form, even if that means performing fewer reps(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/2018-11-15/5-workout-strategies-for-trans-women#:~:text=you%27ll%20reach%20a%20fitness%20plateau,do%20it%20with%20good%20form).

Title: The Best Fitness Apps and Home Workout Programs
Author: Vanessa Caceres
Summary: A roundup of workout apps and programs. Dani Singer points out that if you work with a personal trainer, they may offer on‑demand workouts through their website and schedule virtual classes, giving clients more flexibility(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/best-fitness-apps-and-home-workouts#:~:text=,virtual%20classes%20at%20specific%20times).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer notes that many trainers have on‑demand workouts on their own sites and offer virtual classes, so clients can train remotely(https://health.usnews.com/wellness/fitness/articles/best-fitness-apps-and-home-workouts#:~:text=,virtual%20classes%20at%20specific%20times).

Title: HIIT Workouts You Can Do From the Comfort of Your Own Home
Author: Business Insider staff (attributed to Insider) – name not specified
Summary: This Business Insider article features Dani Singer’s P.A.U.L. method for a 10‑minute home HIIT routine. Singer instructs readers to pick one exercise from each category—Plyometric cardio, Abs, Upper body, Lower body—and perform each for 30 seconds, resting 30 seconds after completing all four exercises. Repeat the circuit until 10 minutes are up(https://www.businessinsider.com/hiit-workouts-you-can-do-at-home-2018-7#:~:text=Certified%20personal%20trainer%2C%20Dani%20Singer%2C,Here%E2%80%99s%20how%20it%20works).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer outlines his P.A.U.L. method: choose one exercise from each category (plyometric cardio, abs, upper‑body, lower‑body), work for 30 seconds on each, rest 30 seconds after one full circuit, and repeat until you hit 10 minutes(https://www.businessinsider.com/hiit-workouts-you-can-do-at-home-2018-7#:~:text=Certified%20personal%20trainer%2C%20Dani%20Singer%2C,Here%E2%80%99s%20how%20it%20works).

Title: Free 4‑Week Beginner Workout Plan
Author: Kickoff coaches (Kickoff blog)
Summary: This Kickoff blog provides a four‑week workout plan. For the dumbbell deadlift, Dani Singer gives step‑by‑step instructions: start with feet hip‑width apart, hold dumbbells at the front of your thighs, hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor and your abs stay tight, then return by squeezing the glutes and pushing hips forward(https://www.trainwithkickoff.com/blog/4-week-beginner-workout-plan#:~:text=For%20instructions%20on%20dumbbell%20deadlifts%2C,CES).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer instructs readers to stand with feet hip‑width apart, hinge at the hips with a slight knee bend until the torso is almost parallel to the floor, and return to the starting position by squeezing the glutes and pushing the hips forward(https://www.trainwithkickoff.com/blog/4-week-beginner-workout-plan#:~:text=For%20instructions%20on%20dumbbell%20deadlifts%2C,CES).

Title: This Is the Best Workout Order to Get the Body You Want
Author: Marissa Laliberte
Summary: This article explains how to structure a workout. Dani Singer advises warming up with light cardio rather than intense sprints, then beginning with strength training to preserve form and energy(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=this%20is%20one%20time%20when,not%20hinder%20it%2C%E2%80%9D%20says%20Singer). He says compound movements (like squats) should come before isolation moves to prevent fatigue and preserve technique(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=During%20strength%20training%2C%20always%20start,lifting%20trick%20to). Singer recommends prioritizing isolation exercises based on individual goals and giving legs their own day because leg exercises are demanding(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=Pick%20your%20priority). He suggests cooling down with a short walk or foam rolling to reflect on the session and relax(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=Instead%20of%20hopping%20straight%20from,more%20about%20%2017%20what).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer tells readers to avoid sprints in the warm‑up; instead, do light cardio and start with strength training so you can keep good form(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=this%20is%20one%20time%20when,not%20hinder%20it%2C%E2%80%9D%20says%20Singer). He advises performing compound lifts before isolation exercises to avoid uneven fatigue(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=During%20strength%20training%2C%20always%20start,lifting%20trick%20to) and stresses giving leg day its own focus because leg exercises require more energy(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=Pick%20your%20priority). During the cool‑down, he suggests a short walk or foam rolling to sense tension and breathe it out(https://www.thehealthy.com/exercise/best-workout-plan/#:~:text=Instead%20of%20hopping%20straight%20from,more%20about%20%2017%20what).

Title: Want a Lean Body? Do This One Exercise Over All Others, Say Experts
Author: Research staff (Eat This, Not That! republished on Foodmady)
Summary: This article highlights experts’ favorite exercises for a lean body. Dani Singer recommends his P.A.U.L. HIIT method. He praises the routine because it only takes 10 minutes, requires no equipment, can be done at home and therefore tends to get done every day. The method involves selecting one exercise from categories (plyometric cardio, abs, upper body, lower body), working for 30 seconds each, resting minimally and repeating for 10 minutes(https://foodmady.com/want-a-lean-body-do-this-one-exercise-over-all-others-say-experts/#:~:text=now%2C%20courtesy%20of%20Dani%20Singer%2C,%E2%80%9D).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer calls the P.A.U.L. method a ‘beautiful routine’ because it takes only 10 minutes, can be done at home with just body weight and makes it easy to exercise daily. He instructs readers to pick one move from each category, perform it for 30 seconds, rest briefly, then repeat until 10 minutes are up(https://foodmady.com/want-a-lean-body-do-this-one-exercise-over-all-others-say-experts/#:~:text=now%2C%20courtesy%20of%20Dani%20Singer%2C,%E2%80%9D).

Title: Fitness Trends That Will Completely Take Over 2022
Author: Ashley Collins
Summary: The List predicts upcoming fitness trends. When asked about walking workouts, Dani Singer notes that walking is a great low‑intensity exercise because you can hold a conversation while doing it. He says walking’s social aspect has grown popular during the COVID‑19 pandemic when people were feeling isolated(https://www.thelist.com/678140/fitness-trends-that-will-completely-take-over-2022/#:~:text=No%20equipment%20or%20gym%20membership,led%20to%20walking%27s%20trending%20status).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer explains that walking allows people to chat and spend time together, making it a popular low‑intensity exercise, especially after periods of pandemic isolation(https://www.thelist.com/678140/fitness-trends-that-will-completely-take-over-2022/#:~:text=No%20equipment%20or%20gym%20membership,led%20to%20walking%27s%20trending%20status).

Title: How To Rest Like An Elite Athlete
Author: Knox Keranen
Summary: This article discusses recovery strategies. Dani Singer emphasizes that rest days should involve active recovery. He recommends using the time to address muscle tension or joint stiffness with mobility drills. One example he gives is the ‘squat to pike’ drill, which targets hip flexors, hamstrings and the lower back(https://marathonhandbook.com/how-to-rest-like-an-elite-athlete/#:~:text=game%2C%E2%80%9D%20said%20Dani%20Singer%2C%20certified,director%20of%20FIT2GO%20Personal%20Training).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says, ‘When an athlete plans a productive rest day, active recovery is the name of the game,’ and suggests mobility drills such as the squat‑to‑pike to loosen tight muscles(https://marathonhandbook.com/how-to-rest-like-an-elite-athlete/#:~:text=game%2C%E2%80%9D%20said%20Dani%20Singer%2C%20certified,director%20of%20FIT2GO%20Personal%20Training).

Title: The Foolproof Guide to Staying in Shape on Business Trips
Author: No author listed
Summary: This travel‑fitness article offers tips for staying in shape when traveling. Dani Singer advises booking hotels with gyms or swimming pools so you can exercise before breakfast. If the hotel lacks a gym, he suggests booking near a park to get a workout in, and he stresses the importance of planning workouts into your travel schedule(https://www.airhelp.com/en/blog/the-foolproof-guide-to-staying-in-shape-on-business-trips/#:~:text=saw%20on%20TV%20at%202am%E2%80%A6,I%20care%20about%20working%20out).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘Make sure you always book a hotel which has a swimming pool or a gym,’ Singer says, adding that if none are available, choose a hotel near a park and exercise before breakfast(https://www.airhelp.com/en/blog/the-foolproof-guide-to-staying-in-shape-on-business-trips/#:~:text=saw%20on%20TV%20at%202am%E2%80%A6,I%20care%20about%20working%20out).

Title: 4 Morning Stretches to Combat Work‑From‑Home Body Stiffness
Author: Lauren Pardee
Summary: PopSugar features a stretching routine for people working at home. Dani Singer contributes two stretches. For the sit‑and‑reach hamstring stretch, he explains that hamstrings stay contracted while sitting and can cause tightness in the lower back; the stretch loosens hamstrings so you can bend and pick things up more easily. For the doorway chest stretch, he says sitting all day causes rounded shoulders; stretching the chest helps open up the front body and improve posture.
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer notes that hamstrings are constantly contracted when you sit, leading to tightness in the lower back; a sit‑and‑reach stretch helps loosen them. He adds that a doorway chest stretch counteracts leaning forward and opens the chest to improve posture.

Title: Secrets of Highly Successful Instructors
Author: ClassPass After Class editors
Summary: In this piece, experienced fitness professionals share advice for new instructors. Dani Singer tells new trainers that listing credentials and qualifications won’t impress clients. Instead, clients care about how the trainer makes them feel and whether the trainer can solve their problem. Singer says he rarely mentions his accolades when meeting new clients and focuses on forging a connection(https://classpass.com/afterclass/secrets-of-highly-successful-instructors/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CNew%20trainers%20feel%20compelled%20to,%E2%80%9D).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘The less you talk about yourself, the more likely [clients] are to establish a connection with you,’ Singer says, noting that clients care more about feeling understood than about a trainer’s fancy certifications(https://classpass.com/afterclass/secrets-of-highly-successful-instructors/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CNew%20trainers%20feel%20compelled%20to,%E2%80%9D).

Title: 50 Tips for Staying Fit Through Your 50s
Author: PeopleOne Health editors (formerly SparkPeople)
Summary: This long list of fitness tips includes guidance from Dani Singer. He says clients in their 50s adhere better to workouts when they have a strong ‘why’—a meaningful reason behind their goal(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/all/50TipsforStayingFitThroughYour50s#:~:text=8.%20Find%20your%20,Personal%20trainer%20Dani%20Singer). He also emphasizes updating your fitness approach with age; what worked in your 20s might not work in your 50s because both physiology and life circumstances change(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/all/50TipsforStayingFitThroughYour50s#:~:text=12.%20Update%20your%20approach.%20,Personal%20trainer%2013%20%20Dani).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer notes that many people blame lack of discipline when the real problem is lack of desire; once clients find a strong enough ‘why,’ adherence improves(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/all/50TipsforStayingFitThroughYour50s#:~:text=8.%20Find%20your%20,Personal%20trainer%20Dani%20Singer). He advises people in their 50s to find a fitness plan that appeals to who they are now rather than what worked decades ago(https://portal.peopleonehealth.com/HealthyLiving/Fitness/all/50TipsforStayingFitThroughYour50s#:~:text=12.%20Update%20your%20approach.%20,Personal%20trainer%2013%20%20Dani).

Title: Menopause and Weight Gain: What You Need to Know
Author: BODi editorial team
Summary: This article examines why menopause is often linked to weight gain. Dani Singer explains that muscle mass decreases during menopause and says the most effective way to combat this is strength training. Cardio still matters, but for menopausal women ‘strength training comes in at number one’(https://www.bodi.com/blog/menopause-and-weight-gain#:~:text=Muscle%20mass%20may%C2%A0decrease%20during%20menopause%2C,certified%20personal%20trainer).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer states that muscle mass tends to decline during menopause and that the best antidote is strength training; cardio remains important, but strength training is the top priority(https://www.bodi.com/blog/menopause-and-weight-gain#:~:text=Muscle%20mass%20may%C2%A0decrease%20during%20menopause%2C,certified%20personal%20trainer).

Title: 4 Healthy Swaps to Help You Lose Weight
Author: MyFitnessPal blog editors
Summary: A weight‑loss tip list for busy people. Dani Singer suggests switching small work meetings to walking meetings. The aim isn’t to sweat but to integrate more natural movement into the day. He notes that walking meetings boost mood and energy beyond the calories burned(https://blog.myfitnesspal.com/4-healthy-swaps-help-lose-weight/#:~:text=The%20Swap%3A%20To%20improve%20your,cognitive%20engagement%20on%20the%20job).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer advises holding walking meetings instead of sitting in an office; the goal is to add more natural movement, not to get sweaty, and the boost in mood and energy is a bonus(https://blog.myfitnesspal.com/4-healthy-swaps-help-lose-weight/#:~:text=The%20Swap%3A%20To%20improve%20your,cognitive%20engagement%20on%20the%20job).

Title: Why the Weight Swings?
Author: Azumio blog editors
Summary: This post explains why body weight fluctuates throughout the day. Dani Singer clarifies that carbs don’t make you fat; they cause water retention, so after eating carbs your weight may increase temporarily(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=%E2%80%9CIf%20you%E2%80%99ve%20had%20a%20lot,%E2%80%9D). He notes that weight can drop after exercise due to water loss but returns after rehydrating(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=Singer%20notes%20exercising%20as%20a,will%20likely%20level%20back%20out). Singer says a safe fat‑loss pace is 1–2 pounds per week and recommends weighing yourself at the same time each day and averaging over a week(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=also%20be%20dangerous,and%20then%20some).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer explains that eating carbohydrates leads to water retention, causing weight to spike even though fat hasn’t increased(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=%E2%80%9CIf%20you%E2%80%99ve%20had%20a%20lot,%E2%80%9D). He notes that immediate weight drops after exercise are usually just water loss(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=Singer%20notes%20exercising%20as%20a,will%20likely%20level%20back%20out). To track progress, he recommends aiming for 1–2 pounds of weight loss per week and averaging daily weigh‑ins taken at the same time of day(https://www.azumio.com/blog/health/why-you-weigh-different-throughout-the-day#:~:text=also%20be%20dangerous,and%20then%20some).

Title: 11 Weight‑Loss Rules Meant to Be Broken
Author: SparkPeople editors
Summary: This article busts common weight‑loss myths. Dani Singer targets the rule that you shouldn’t eat after 8 p.m., explaining that from a weight‑loss perspective 100 calories at midnight is the same as 100 calories at lunchtime; the only benefit of the rule is limiting total daily calories(https://www.sparkpeople.com/resource/motivation_articles.asp#:~:text=4,M).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says the ‘don’t eat after 8 p.m.’ rule is often misinterpreted; calories consumed at midnight count the same as those eaten earlier, so the rule’s only real use is limiting total calorie intake(https://www.sparkpeople.com/resource/motivation_articles.asp#:~:text=4,M).

Title: 6 Tips for Keeping Your Resolutions on Track
Author: SparkPeople editors
Summary: A New‑Year‑resolution guide. Dani Singer advises breaking big goals into small, specific habits. He says an hour‑long workout may not be realistic for busy people, so starting with a ten‑minute morning walk or preparing lunch the night before can make resolutions stick(https://www.sparkpeople.com/blog/blog.asp#:~:text=Get%20super%20small%E2%80%94and%20super%20specific).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer suggests setting small, specific habits—such as a 10‑minute morning walk or prepping lunch each night—to make resolutions sustainable when hour‑long workouts aren’t realistic(https://www.sparkpeople.com/blog/blog.asp#:~:text=Get%20super%20small%E2%80%94and%20super%20specific).

Title: 12 Elliptical Mistakes That Can Sabotage Your Workout
Author: Chelsea Piers Playbook editors (Chelsea Piers: The Playbook)
Summary: This Playbook piece outlines common mistakes on the elliptical machine. Dani Singer argues that fat‑burning heart‑rate zones are a myth: weight loss is about burning calories, whether they come from carbs or fat. He says if you want to lose weight, focus on total calories burned rather than the type of fuel your body uses(https://playbook.chelseapiers.com/news/12-elliptical-mistakes-that-can-sabotage-your-workout/#:~:text=calories,gym%20mistakes%2C%20which).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘Whether you’re burning carbs or fat is irrelevant—weight loss is about the calories that you’re burning,’ Singer explains(https://playbook.chelseapiers.com/news/12-elliptical-mistakes-that-can-sabotage-your-workout/#:~:text=calories,gym%20mistakes%2C%20which).

Title: 16 Rude Gym Habits You Need to Stop Doing ASAP
Author: Readers’ Digest editors
Summary: A list of common gym etiquette mistakes. Dani Singer advises gym‑goers not to stand directly in front of the weight rack while lifting. Doing so blocks others from accessing the dumbbells; instead, grab the weights you need and move to an open spot(https://www.rd.com/list/things-to-never-do-at-the-gym/#:~:text=There%E2%80%99s%20an%20unspoken%20%E2%80%9Cno,workout%2C%20you%20just%20might%20find).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer says that starting a set of biceps curls in front of the weight rack blocks the entire gym from accessing the weights and recommends grabbing what you need and finding an open spot(https://www.rd.com/list/things-to-never-do-at-the-gym/#:~:text=There%E2%80%99s%20an%20unspoken%20%E2%80%9Cno,workout%2C%20you%20just%20might%20find).

Title: How Your Personality Type Can Boost Workout Motivation, Per Study
Author: Korin Miller
Summary: Women’s Health covers research linking personality traits to exercise adherence. Dani Singer says top trainers don’t overlook the ‘personal’ aspect of personal training. They may train multiple clients with the same goal using different personality‑friendly modalities(https://www.womenshealthmag.com/health/a65415167/personality-type-workout-motivation-study/#:~:text=This%20is%20crucial%20for%20sticking,friendly%E2%80%99%20modalities.%E2%80%9D).
Notable quotes by Dani: ‘Trainers who consistently achieve the best results with their clients don’t overlook the personal aspect of personal training … They often train multiple clients with the same fitness goal, using different “trait‑friendly” modalities’(https://www.womenshealthmag.com/health/a65415167/personality-type-workout-motivation-study/#:~:text=This%20is%20crucial%20for%20sticking,friendly%E2%80%99%20modalities.%E2%80%9D).

Title: Underrated Exercises You’re Probably Not Doing
Author: Health Digest editors
Summary: Health Digest highlights lesser‑known moves. Dani Singer notes that many people are knee‑dominant when they squat because sitting all day trains the body to lead with the knees. He recommends the kneeling squat, which teaches hip flexion and extension and carries over to proper squats(https://www.healthdigest.com/316803/underrated-exercises-youre-probably-not-doing/#:~:text=muscle%20,carry%20over%20to%20your%20squats).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer explains that people tend to be knee‑dominant when squatting due to prolonged sitting; the kneeling squat trains hip flexion/extension and improves squat mechanics(https://www.healthdigest.com/316803/underrated-exercises-youre-probably-not-doing/#:~:text=muscle%20,carry%20over%20to%20your%20squats).

Title: Strong Fitness Magazine, Issue 32 (Jan/Feb 2019) – ‘Simplify Your Morning with HIIT’
Author: Strong Fitness Magazine editors
Summary: In this issue’s ‘Simplify Your Morning’ section, Dani Singer suggests beginning every day with a focused 10‑minute HIIT workout before even checking your phone. He compares this habit to brushing your teeth and argues that it creates consistency and ensures exercise doesn’t get skipped.
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer tells readers to start each morning with a 10‑minute HIIT session before looking at their phone, likening the ritual to brushing your teeth.

Title: Strong Fitness Magazine, Issue 37 (Nov/Dec 2019) – ‘Food Shaming’
Author: Strong Fitness Magazine editors
Summary: An article about diet culture and food shaming. Dani Singer states that shaming someone about their food choices is not only wrong but also ineffective; guilt rarely inspires lasting change.
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer argues that food shaming backfires because it makes people less likely to change, so coaches should avoid using guilt as a tactic.

Title: Fitness and Recovery Tips for Senior Men (article from LifeLine)
Author: LifeLine editors (seniors’ health blog)
Summary: This comprehensive guide for senior men includes extensive commentary from Dani Singer. He cautions that improper exercise form leads to knee, hip or back pain and emphasizes that seniors often feel stronger once their form is corrected(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=). Singer says strength training reduces loss of muscle mass and bone density and suggests consulting a professional(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CStrength%20training%20is%20one%20of,set%20of%20exercises%20for%20you). He recommends squats for mobility(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20Singer%20says%20squats,the%20ability%20to%20get%20around), standing on one leg to reduce fall risk(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20Singer%20says%20you,down%2C%20ramp%20up%20the%20difficulty) and at least 30 minutes of activity per day for heart health(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20%E2%80%9C,%E2%80%9D). He endorses yoga for stress relief and mind‑body connection(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20%E2%80%9CIt%E2%80%99s%20good%20for,body%20connection%2C%20and) and encourages combining strength training with adequate protein to combat muscle and bone loss(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Combine%20strength%20training%20and%20protein,train%20and%20to%20consume%20adequate). He also mentions glute bridges to balance leg muscles(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20Singer%20likes%20the,and%20back%20of%20the%20leg).
Notable quotes by Dani: Singer warns that poor exercise form causes knee, hip or back pain and that seniors often feel stronger once they correct it(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=). He emphasizes that strength training is key to preserving muscle and bone density(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CStrength%20training%20is%20one%20of,set%20of%20exercises%20for%20you) and recommends squats for mobility(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20Singer%20says%20squats,the%20ability%20to%20get%20around), balance drills like standing on one leg to prevent falls(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20Singer%20says%20you,down%2C%20ramp%20up%20the%20difficulty) and daily activity for heart health(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20%E2%80%9C,%E2%80%9D). He points out that yoga helps relieve stress and build body awareness(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Bonus%20Tip%3A%20%E2%80%9CIt%E2%80%99s%20good%20for,body%20connection%2C%20and) and says seniors should combine strength training with adequate protein intake to fight muscle and bone loss(https://www.lifeline.com/blog/train-smart-recover-fast-tips-for-active-senior-men/#:~:text=Combine%20strength%20training%20and%20protein,train%20and%20to%20consume%20adequate).

Title: How Weight Loss Changes as You Age (Weight Loss in Your 30s section)

Summary: This article discusses weight loss at various ages. In the 30s section, Dani Singer says weight‑loss success hinges on creative, practical planning.
